analysis.investment_thesis: Castrol India is the closest thing to a Magic Formula stock in this batch: earnings yield of 7.3% (EBIT ₹1,292 Cr / EV ₹17,665 Cr) clears my 6% floor, and ROCE of 68% is exceptional for any business. The friction is structural — lubricant volumes face a multi-year headwind from EV adoption, capping revenue growth at just 6.2% CAGR, which limits how aggressively I want to size a position.
key_strengths: ROCE of ~68% and FCF margin of ~17% (₹993 Cr FCF on ₹5,700 Cr revenue) — extraordinarily capital-efficient business with near-zero capex intensity (capex only ₹97 Cr, 1.7% of revenue)
EV/EBITDA of 12.6× is the most reasonable valuation in this cohort, and earnings yield of 7.3% passes the Magic Formula threshold
Durable brand moat (Castrol EDGE, MAGNATEC, Activ) with a pan-India distribution network protecting pricing power and operating margin of 24.9%
key_risks: Revenue CAGR of only 6.2% (FY22–FY25) — Electric Vehicles structurally reduce engine oil consumption; growth ceiling is compressing
As a 51%-held subsidiary of Castrol Ltd UK, strategic decisions (pricing, capex, dividends) serve parent interests — minority investors face governance risk
Finance cost growing at 32% CAGR even on minimal debt — rising lease obligations could erode the asset-light thesis over time
red_flags: ROE of 0.45% appears anomalous given ₹950 Cr net profit and ₹1,900 Cr equity — likely a data artefact from mid-year dividend reductions; investors should verify equity base used in the calculation
Financing CF of -₹1,315 Cr in FY25 suggests near-total profit distribution — limited reinvestment signals management does not see high-ROIC growth opportunities domestically
EV transition risk is real but unquantified — no visibility into how quickly oil volume erosion offsets premium product premiumisation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula scores: Earnings yield = ₹1,292 Cr / ₹17,665 Cr EV = 7.31% — above my 6% threshold. ROCE = 68% — exceptional, well above my 20% minimum. This is a genuine two-for-one Magic Formula candidate, and by that framework it deserves a positive lean. The capex intensity (₹97 Cr on ₹5,700 Cr revenue) is among the lowest I have seen, and OCF conversion (₹1,090 Cr OCF vs ₹950 Cr net profit) confirms the earnings are real cash.

However, I assign a HOLD rather than BUY because the low-growth profile (6.2% revenue CAGR) and structural EV headwind mean the earnings yield will improve slowly, if at all. The company is essentially a mature cash cow being steadily milked by its UK parent (₹1,315 Cr financing outflows in FY25). I would upgrade to BUY if the stock re-rated below 10× EV/EBITDA (implying EV ~₹14,040 Cr, ~20% lower), which would push earnings yield above 9%.
